paper.title: Effects of annealing temperature on microstructure and mechanical properties of a low density δ-TRIP steel plate via intercritical quenching-annealing process
paper.paper_scope: This study investigates the effect of intercritical annealing temperature (620–800 °C after intercritical quenching at 1050 °C) on the micro-laminated microstructure (δ-ferrite band + tempered martensite + retained/reverted austenite), austenitic stability, TRIP/TWIP deformation behavior, and tensile mechanical properties of a low-density Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C (wt.%) δ-TRIP steel plate.

alloys.description: A low-density δ-TRIP (transformation-induced plasticity) steel prepared as a 5 kg ingot by vacuum induction furnace, used to study the effect of intercritical quenching-annealing on microstructure and mechanical properties. It features a dual-phase micro-laminated microstructure of δ-ferrite band and martensite/austenite due to the Al and Mn additions.
alloys.alloys_notes: Design/nominal composition stated as Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C (wt.%) throughout the text. The actual measured chemical composition (Table 1) is Fe-8.9Mn-4.6Al-0.29C with P and S each < 0.005 wt.%. Density is 7.34 g·cm-3 (by Archimedes drainage method), 6.7 % lower than low-carbon low-alloyed steels.

source.reason: The abstract and introduction define the single experimental steel as Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C (wt.%) low density steel; the composition is quantified in Table 1 and the ingot preparation is described in the experiments section. All treatment states (HR, IQ, QA) belong to this same composition, so only one alloy entity is defined.

processes.description: Ingot reheated to 1100 °C for 2 h, hot rolled from 80 to 12 mm in eight passes (initial rolling temperature ~1050 °C, finishing rolling temperature ~950 °C), then air cooled to room temperature.

source.reason: The experiments section defines the hot-rolled reference state: after reheating the forging ingot and hot rolling, the plate was air cooled to room temperature and the corresponding sample labeled HR.

processes.description: Hot-rolled plate reheated to 1050 °C (ferrite + austenite dual-phase region) for 1 h, followed by water quenching; sample labeled IQ-1050.

source.reason: The experiments section describes the intercritical quenching treatment of the hot-rolled plate at 1050 °C for 1 h followed by water quenching, with sample labeled IQ-1050.

processes.description: Water-quenched plate (IQ-1050) annealed for 1 h at 620 °C (below the A1 cementite precipitation temperature ~617 °C), with carbides precipitated in the tempered martensite.
processes.processes_notes: One of four annealing temperatures (620, 680, 740, 800 °C) applied for 1 h to the same water-quenched IQ-1050 plate; annealing at 620 °C is the only condition where carbides precipitate.

source.reason: The experiments section lists the water-quenched plate annealed for 1 h at 620 °C with the corresponding sample labeled QA-620; Table 3 and Fig. 6 confirm QA-620 as a distinct treatment state.

processes.description: Water-quenched plate (IQ-1050) annealed for 1 h at 680 °C; exhibits the highest austenitic stability and lowest k value, with deficient TRIP effect and necking.
processes.processes_notes: One of four annealing temperatures (620, 680, 740, 800 °C) applied for 1 h to the same water-quenched IQ-1050 plate.

source.reason: The experiments section lists the water-quenched plate annealed for 1 h at 680 °C with the corresponding sample labeled QA-680; Table 3 confirms QA-680 as a distinct treatment state.

processes.description: Water-quenched plate (IQ-1050) annealed for 1 h at 740 °C; exhibits the maximum austenite fraction transformed during deformation, highest uniform elongation (~62.4 %) and highest PSE (~45.2 GPa%).
processes.processes_notes: One of four annealing temperatures (620, 680, 740, 800 °C) applied for 1 h to the same water-quenched IQ-1050 plate.

source.reason: The experiments section lists the water-quenched plate annealed for 1 h at 740 °C with the corresponding sample labeled QA-740; Table 3 confirms QA-740 as a distinct treatment state.

processes.description: Water-quenched plate (IQ-1050) annealed for 1 h at 800 °C; small austenite grains grow and alloy elements dilute, causing partial martensitic transformation during air cooling and newly formed martensite in the tempered martensite region.
processes.processes_notes: One of four annealing temperatures (620, 680, 740, 800 °C) applied for 1 h to the same water-quenched IQ-1050 plate; the only annealed state where partial austenite transforms to martensite during air cooling.

source.reason: The experiments section lists the water-quenched plate annealed for 1 h at 800 °C with the corresponding sample labeled QA-800; Table 3 and Fig. 3(h) confirm QA-800 as a distinct treatment state.
The hot-rolled plate of the Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C steel air-cooled to room temperature is labeled HR and constitutes one alloy+process sample.
The intercritically quenched (1050 °C/1 h + water quench) specimen of the Fe–9Mn–5Al–0.3C steel is labeled IQ-1050 and constitutes one alloy+process sample.
The IQ-1050 plate annealed at 620 °C for 1 h is labeled QA-620 and constitutes one alloy+process sample with distinct mechanical properties and precipitated carbides.
The IQ-1050 plate annealed at 680 °C for 1 h is labeled QA-680 and constitutes one alloy+process sample with the highest austenitic stability among the QA series.
The IQ-1050 plate annealed at 740 °C for 1 h is labeled QA-740 and constitutes one alloy+process sample with the highest PSE and uniform elongation.
The IQ-1050 plate annealed at 800 °C for 1 h is labeled QA-800 and constitutes one alloy+process sample exhibiting martensite formed during air cooling.

unmapped_findings: Measured density of the experimental steel is 7.34 g·cm-3 (Archimedes drainage method), 6.7 % lower than that of low-carbon low-alloyed steels.

Thermo-Calc (TCFE12 database) equilibrium calculation: δ-ferrite (BCC_A2) precipitates from liquid at ~1485 °C; austenite (FCC_A1) forms by peritectic reaction at ~1390 °C; austenite fraction reaches a maximum of ~91.4 % at ~970 °C while δ-ferrite reaches a minimum of ~8.6 %; the A1 cementite precipitation temperature is ~617 °C.

Estimated stacking fault energies (SFE) of the QA specimens are all between 20 and 40 mJ/m2 (QA-620 ~36.50, QA-680 ~38.27, QA-740 ~33.29, QA-800 ~31.53 mJ/m2), implying TWIP effect could operate during deformation.
Austenitic mechanical stability constant k values: QA-740 ~1.47 and QA-800 ~1.50 (highest, more notable TRIP effect), QA-680 ~0.56 (lowest, little austenite-to-martensite transformation).

The experimental steel after QA treatment is suggested as a third-generation advanced high-strength steel that could substitute for TRIP 590T/400Y (SAE J2745-2007) or TRIP 580T/400Y high-strength automobile plates.
